The energy density and angular distribution of power radiated by a quark undergoing circular motion in strongly coupled N=4 super Yang-Mills theory is computed using gauge/gravity duality.
The results are qualitatively similar to synchrotron radiation produced by an electron in circular motion in classical electrodynamics.
At large velocities, the quark emits radiation in a narrow beam along its velocity vector with a characteristic opening angle scaling as 1/γ and radial thickness scaling as 1/γ^3.
The shape of the rotating string in the gravitational description is uniquely determined by the solutions to the Euler-Lagrange equations for the Nambu-Goto action.

The analytical expression for the energy density involves several terms depending on the retarded time, the radial distance, the velocity and acceleration of the quark, and trigonometric functions of the angular coordinates.
In the far zone (r → ∞), the angular distribution of the time-averaged radiated power is focused about θ = π/2 with a characteristic width scaling as 1/γ.
The total radiated power agrees with the vacuum result, even for a test quark moving through a strongly coupled plasma at finite temperature.
The authors attribute the negative energy density observed before and after the pulse of radiation to quantum effects.
Previous studies have shown isotropization of radiation in strongly coupled gauge theories, but the results in this paper do not exhibit any isotropization.
Studying the radiation from a circulating quark in this strongly coupled gauge theory provides insights into the behavior of radiation in a non-abelian, strongly coupled quantum field theory.

The results open the way to new methods of modeling jet quenching in heavy ion collisions by studying how the tightly collimated beam of synchrotron radiation interacts with the strongly coupled plasma.
The gravitational description in AdS space is used to calculate the energy density and angular distribution of the radiation in the dual quantum field theory.
The rotating motion of the string dual to the quark creates gravitational radiation which propagates up to the boundary of the AdS geometry, inducing a 4D stress tensor.
The energy density is calculated by solving the linearized Einstein equations, with the 5D string stress tensor as the source.
The authors find that the radiation pattern does not exhibit any isotropization, in contrast to previous studies on the isotropization of radiation in strongly coupled gauge theories.
